assertion: CMS finalized a rule implementing H.R. 1 immigrant eligibility limits, and thousands of lawfully present immigrants will be terminated from Medicare in early 2027, starting February 1, 2027.
independent_value: Proposed rule (CMS-1848-P, July 16, 2026) confirmed on Justice in Aging page and Federal Register link; search results report final CY2027 PFS rule (CMS-1848-F) with Feb 1, 2027 terminations; I did not read the final rule text. Estimates of affected people range from ~32,000 (CMS Actuary, per one outlet) to ~300,000 notices.

sources.title: JIA template comments on proposed rule

reason: Statute and proposal verified; final-rule text not read.

assertion: Newly ineligible groups include refugees, asylees, TPS holders; only LPRs, certain Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA residents remain eligible.
independent_value: JIA page: eligibility limited to citizens, nationals, LPRs, Cuban/Haitian entrants, COFA; TPS holders, refugees, asylees no longer eligible.

assertion: Major insurers are cutting Medicare Advantage supplemental dental benefits for 2027.
independent_value: Leerink analysis via Healthcare Dive (Oct 1, 2026): UnitedHealthcare dental cuts hit ~70% of members, Centene 45%, CVS/Aetna 36%, Elevance 23%; Humana modestly increased dental allowances. STAT also reports drastic dental cuts. CMS characterizes market as stable.

assertion: In NFHA's 2026 Fair Housing Trends Report, HUD did not provide requested data, the first time that has happened in the report's history.
independent_value: NFHA 2026 report highlights: 'Critical federal data missing for the first time since 1996'; HUD and DOJ did not provide requested data.

assertion: HUD's attempts to defund nonprofit fair housing agencies forced service cuts and staff reductions; nonprofits handle more than 75% of fair housing complaints.
independent_value: NFHA: 76% of reporting member orgs had funding disruptions, many cut services; FHIP zeroed out in administration budget. The 75% figure was not found on the 2026 highlights page; an earlier NFHA citation ties ~75% to FHIP grantees, not nonprofits generally.
